children: Canada real estate firm's Q1 revenue rose slightly year-over-year on higher property revenue
Net income per share for Q1 fell sharply from prior year due to lower one-time gains
Adjusted funds from operations per share declined year-over-year
Company did not provide specific guidance or outlook for future quarters or the full year
PROPERTY REVENUE - Slight increase in property revenue contributed to higher total revenue
ONE-TIME GAIN ABSENCE - Net income fell mainly due to the absence of prior-year expropriation settlement proceeds
HIGHER ADMIN COSTS AND FAIR VALUE ADJUSTMENT - Increased administrative expenses and an unfavorable change in fair value adjustment also weighed on net income
